learning_outcomes.text: Students expand their understanding of the development and application of human-machine cooperation systems by integrating technological, ergonomic, and ethical aspects to deal with future challenges safely and responsibly.
They deepen their expertise in functional safety, usability, and ethics to design user-oriented and ethically justifiable cooperation systems that meet current technological standards.

Students can design human-machine cooperation systems by applying learned concepts, including technical, ergonomic, and ethical aspects, to develop user-centered and safe solutions. They are also able to reflect on the effectiveness and appropriateness of the designed systems to continuously improve their usability, trustworthiness, and functional safety.

Students can shape scientific innovations to advance human-machine cooperation by developing novel concepts for technology and interaction. They are able to question existing approaches and propose evidence-based improvements that increase the effectiveness, safety, and usability of cooperation systems.

Students are able to effectively communicate the importance and impact of human-machine cooperation by presenting complex technological and ergonomic concepts understandably to an interdisciplinary audience and highlighting the relevance of ethical considerations in the design of such systems. They can actively work in teams and contribute interdisciplinary knowledge to jointly develop innovative solutions that optimize the interaction between humans and machines, thereby overcoming safety, trustworthiness, and usability challenges.

syllabus_topics: Definitions, historical development and current state of technology
Fundamentals of Human-Machine Interaction (HMI), Human Factors Engineering, Explainability, Trustworthiness and Safety
Ergonomic design of interfaces and control elements considering: Explainability, Trustworthiness and Safety
Usability and User Experience in safety-critical mechatronic systems
Design Thinking approaches for the development of safety-relevant solutions
Social and societal impacts of cooperative systems (dependence, addiction, accessibility, legislation, access to technology, etc.)
bibliography: Various current scientific articles and treatises.
